01 // The engineering challenge

Temperature and flow are coupled

  • Temperature alters the density and drives buoyancy, buoyancy alters the velocity, and the velocity transports the temperature.
  • Recurrence CFD (rCFD) replays recorded flow data instead of solving the momentum equations again.
  • Valid as long as the temperature does not act back on the flow.

Research questions

  1. Where does the replay remain accurate?
  2. Where does it fail?
  3. How can it be improved?

The feedback loop of a buoyant temperaturereference CFD against replay

02 // The rCFD approach

Record, replay, correct

  1. Record. A CFD run stores the recorded motion as cell-to-cell maps.
  2. Replay. The maps transport the temperature, without the momentum equations.
  3. Correct. Face exchange adds mixing, a correction reduces numerical diffusion, global conservation keeps the energy balance.

Guiding principle

A replay cannot contain physical processes that are absent from its database.

04 // Where the standard replay breaks down

One mixing parameter, two competing objectives

  • More mixing improves the height of the heat, up to fsd ≈ 0.5.
  • More mixing also adds numerical diffusion.
  • The smeared thermocline lets extra heat leave through the outlet.

No single face-exchange strength optimises both measures.

Stronger mixing makes the replay too warm during the inflow and too cold after it. Black dashed, reference. Light blue, stronger fsd.

05 // Diagnosis

The smearing comes from face exchange, not from the recorded motion

  • Recorded maps alone keep the thermocline 2 to 4 mm thin.
  • Standard replay: 15.7 mm at 599 s, three times the reference.
  • Face exchange at fsd = 0.5 acts like ten times the molecular diffusivity, about 20 mm after two minutes.
  • The reference is stably stratified, N = 5.8 s−1. Face exchange mixes equally in all directions.

Rows: reference, maps only, standard replay, extended replay. Numbers: 10–90 % thickness on the centre line.

06 // The extended replay

Restoring the thermocline without violating local temperature bounds

  • Conservative exchange between neighbouring cells.
  • Directional weighting across the thermocline.
  • A local-bounds limiter of the Zalesak type.
  • The global energy constraint is retained.

08 // The limit: missing motion

A local correction cannot create a convective motion that was never recorded

  • The lid removes heat, and the cooled liquid becomes denser and sinks.
  • First test, the adiabatic database under the cooled lid. Its recording contains no sinking motion.
  • The replay removes only 63 % of the reference lid heat loss, and 64 to 67 % with stronger mixing or the correction.

So

The database must hold the flow regime. I recorded it again, this time under cooling.

mid-plane, cooled lid

referencecooled liquid sinks, the upper layer mixes

10 // The limit of local corrections

What no local rule can fix: the filling lag

  • During the warm inflow the heterogeneity lags by 2.25 K, and the traces meet only after the inflow.
  • Four variants change nothing: wall multiplier, Richardson weight, several passes, reversed weight.
  • Heat is in the wrong layer at the wrong time, so this is a transport error.
  • Diagnostic only: the recorded convective flux gives 2.25 → 0.45 K, but the run ends 0.86 K too cold.

The flux is not part of the method. The excess cooling arises where it meets the single-compartment conservation constraint.

13 // Contributions

What this thesis establishes

1Quantifies the mixing and energy trade-off of the standard replay, through the outlet below the thermocline.
2Traces the smearing to face exchange and develops a bounded, vertically weighted correction.
3Shows that the database must hold the flow regime, here the convection driven by the cooled lid.
4Shows the limit of local corrections: the remaining filling lag is a transport error.
5Transfers the operators to a through-flow vessel, with settings chosen per feed.
14 // Limitations and next steps

Each limitation defines the next step

Current limitationNext step
Accuracy depends on the coverage of the recorded database.→Databases that cover several flow regimes.
Flow structures absent from the database cannot be reconstructed.→Physics-informed representation of the missing transport.
Correction settings are selected per case.→Automatic or learned selection of the correction settings.

The goal is not to replace CFD, but to make existing CFD knowledge more reusable.

Scope: one closed configuration, one mesh and one vessel. The references are simulations.

15 // Conclusion

A recorded flow can transport a non-passive temperature, within the limits of its recorded motion

1Correct numerical diffusion where it occurs.
2Preserve the physical transport the database represents.
3Do not expect local corrections to rebuild missing flow dynamics.

Thank you for your attention.

B5 // Backup · Limits

What the study does not show

Reference and case

The closed-configuration reference is a laminar simulation at Re ≈ 100, not a measurement. One mesh and one set of physical parameters, no discretisation-uncertainty study. The fluid has a Prandtl number near 42. The working strengths belong to it.

Replay and vessel

All three databases are non-recurrent, so no replay extrapolates in time. The saving of about 260× counts the replay alone. The floor-fed replays run the lid-fed frames on their own clock, 24.5 s later. The effect of this offset was not tested.

B8 // Backup · Standard replay

Why not replay the maps alone

Mid-plane, four instants, adiabaticmaps only, no face exchange

thermocline thickness240 s315 s599 s reference4.56.05.0 mmmaps only2.51.94.3 mmstandard, fsd = 0.519.319.815.7 mm
  • The maps alone keep the thermocline as thin as the reference, or thinner. They are not the source of the numerical diffusion.
  • Without face exchange the replay lacks subgrid-scale mixing. The upper layer keeps unmixed pockets, and the centre-of-gravity error nearly doubles, 0.116 mm at fsd = 0 against 0.068 mm at 0.5.
  • The jet needs face exchange, the thermocline does not. The extended replay keeps it and corrects only across the thermocline.

02 // Two time scales

The flow settles in seconds, the heat takes minutes

CFD must resolve the fast flow time scale throughout the entire process. Digital twins and parameter studies require results within minutes.

The same pattern appears in a hot-water store, a ladle of molten steel or a chemical reactor. Right, the reference run of this thesis.

11 // Q3 · Cooled lid

The database must be recorded under cooling

Heat leaves through the lid only as fast as the flow brings warm fluid to it. With a database recorded under an adiabatic lid, the replay removes only 63 % of the reference heat loss.

Wall term on the top cell row: q = h A (T − Tamb), h = 100 W/(m² K), Tamb = 293 K. A fair comparison needs the same flow in both stages and the same instant.

Heat removed through the lidreference = 100 %

18 // Future work

The correction strength is the first candidate for a learned model

The strength was selected by parameter studies for each case. A recurrence database holds many states of the same flow and is therefore a suitable basis for learning.

First step
Learned correction strength

A small network predicts the local strength from the replayed field. It acts inside the limiter, so conservation and the local bounds are kept.

Sparse sensors
Energy-equation residual

A loss based on the residual of the energy equation could use sparse measurements, such as the vessel thermocouples.

Missing motion
Database switching

Separate databases for different flow regimes, selected from the replayed temperature.

None of these extensions was tested in this thesis. Larger field-to-field models would need many paired states and provide no bounds.
